Cristian Chivu warns Inter ‘failed the exam’ in their 4-4 draw with Atalanta, criticising some of his players. ‘We were too soft, need to be more determined in the duels.’.

The Nerazzurri performed several remarkable comebacks this season, but they were on the wrong end of it tonight in Bergamo after fumbling a two-goal advantage three times.

Pio Esposito scored his first ever Serie A hat-trick, carrying on the remarkable form seen for Italy in the Nations League, and the Petar Sucic penalty had seemingly put the game to bed at 4-2.

However, Charles De Ketelaere’s second of the game and a Franck spot-kick in stoppages allowed Atalanta to claw their way back for 4-4.

“We were leading 2-0, 3-1 and 4-2, so this is the regret,” Chivu told DAZN Italia.

“We had an idea of what we should’ve done and did not do, we should’ve controlled the advantage, then when we felt them snapping at our heels, we immediately restored the two-goal cushion.

According to recent reports, “I think we failed the exam in the final minutes. It’s hard to say why we were unable to control the lead. We have to congratulate Atalanta, as they sensed that we were a bit shallow, and pumped crosses into the box, put bodies in there, while we were a little soft compared to our usual approach.

“I’m sorry, I see this as two gifted points, but we will learn from it and know now to let the intensity and mentality drop in the next games.”.

Inter were angry at the Davide Zappacosta penalty for clearing off the line with his elbow because it was only a yellow card and not a red.

Alessandro Bastoni also felt the decisive spot-kick was harsh, but while his handball was unintentional, the arms were raised above his shoulder and therefore in a punishable position.

“The second Atalanta goal came from a corner, identical to one where Pepo had just made a great save moments earlier, so we did not learn from it,” continued Chivu.

Industry observers note that “When we got to 4-2, our defence was then static in a chaotic situation. We need a certain determination and focus in these situations, and we were negligent in that area today.”.

There was another serious blow today along with the dropped points, because Hakan Calhanoglu limped off with a suspected flexor strain in the first half.

At least Curtis Jones and Lautaro Martinez made their comebacks after more than a month out, two in the case of the former Liverpool midfielder.

Industry observers note that “I felt we were suffering on the wings, partly because we were too soft, we were allowing the space to put the crosses in too easily. I decided to put Marcus Thuram wide to help out Djed Spence in the final stages,” explained Chivu.

“It’s a matter of desire to go into the duels, to be more determined, not just put bodies behind the ball, because if you don’t have the right intensity then a single error can be costly.”.

Inter have conceded 17 goals in 12 Serie A games, more than any other side in the top six, but this is their first draw of the entire season after 11 wins and three defeats in all competition.

Is Chivu more angry at the dropped points, or worried at how many goals Inter are conceding this season?

In a recent development, “We are conceding too many goals for a club that has high ambitions, but we must do like we did in Rotterdam and with Como, respond to a setback, not look over our shoulders to the past. We must learn that we cannot just control a situation, we’ve got to keep giving 100 per cent until the final whistle,” concluded the Inter coach.

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers are beginning to show how neurons in the brain detect an infection and tailor physiological responses to fight it.Credit: Dr.
  • Sources indicate that A viral cold or bacterial infection can leave you feeling miserable, but each infection produces its own mix of symptoms.
  • It has been revealed that the findings, many of which are unpublished, were presented on 15 November at the Society for Neuroscience annual meeting in Washington DC, and challenge the established view of what it means to feel unwell.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers are beginning to show how neurons in the brain detect an infection and tailor physiological responses to fight it.Credit: Dr. Chris Henstridge/SPL.

Sources indicate that A viral cold or bacterial infection can leave you feeling miserable, but each infection produces its own mix of symptoms. Now, neuroscientists are discovering that the brain is the conductor of these responses — decoding the type of pathogen that has invaded, accessing memories of past bouts of illness and even mobilizing immune defences at the sight of a sick person.

It has been revealed that the findings, many of which are unpublished, were presented on 15 November at the Society for Neuroscience annual meeting in Washington DC, and challenge the established view of what it means to feel unwell. Neuroscientists have long viewed neurological responses to infection as a one-size-fits-all response to inflammation, rather than a strategy tailored to the threat.

“Sickness is actually not a fixed program, although we often talk about it this way,” noted Jessica Osterhout, a neurobiologist at the University of Utah in Salt Lake City, who chaired the session.

Sources indicate that A bacterial infection and a cold caused by a virus can both result in fever and exhaustion, yet they rarely trigger the same constellation of symptoms. Bacterial infections, for instance, tend to suppress appetite much more sharply than do colds, which made Osterhout and her colleagues wonder how the brain tells various pathogens apart.

Your brain could be controlling how sick you get — and how you recover.

Your brain could be controlling how sick you get — and how you recover.

In unpublished experiments, Osterhout’s team compared mice injected with a bacterial toxin with those given a compound that mimics a viral infection. To see how the brain distinguished between pathogens, the researchers profiled individual cells in circumventricular organs, which are specialized structures with unusually permeable blood vessels that surround brain ventricles.

When the body has an infection, cells in the circumventricular organs switch on sets of immune-related genes and release distinct mixes of chemical signals. Those signals diffuse to nearby neurons and create distinct patterns of activity for different pathogens, allowing the brain to customize its symptom profile depending on the threat.

Rather than acting as conduits that let inflammatory signals pass unchecked from the blood into the wider brain, these structures “may actually interpret them”, Osterhout noted.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes, the brain doesn’t even wait for pathogens to enter the body to rally the immune system1. Andrea Serino, a neuroscientist at Lausanne University Hospital in Switzerland, studies how the brain maps peripersonal space, which is the area around the body roughly in arm’s reach.

Sources indicate that when Serino’s team placed volunteers in virtual reality, they found that threat-monitoring brain regions became active when avatars bearing skin lesions caused by viral or bacterial infections approached, even when the figures were beyond arm’s reach. Just 15 minutes of virtual exposure triggered a surge in frontline immune ‘sentinel’ cells in participants’ blood comparable to that induced by an influenza vaccine. This reaction did not occur when participants saw healthy-looking avatars or ones expressing fear.

These experiments suggest that the immune system uses “the predictive ability of the brain to react before pathogens enter the body”, Serino said.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

According to recent reports, back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

In a recent development, fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Both games kick-off at 20:00, with team news coming imminently.

Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Big Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.
  • Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.

Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.

Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.

One problem for Andoni Iraola is his side's frailties in the bigger games, which comes into focus this weekend with United in town – despite the desire to make an easy joke about how this is a clash against relegation fodder.

Since thrashing United 7-0 in 2023, Liverpool have beaten their friends in Manchester just once in seven meetings, including two draws and a defeat at Anfield.

Industry observers note that to use a cliche, form seems to go out of the window for this fixture. In the last two Anfield meetings, Liverpool have been first and second in the table, United 14th and then tenth. This weekend, it is fourth against 18th, though Pochettino’s side could be bottom by kick-off.

Liverpool’s struggles in bigger games stretch further. Against the so-called 'Big Six’, the Reds have won just two of 12 games since winning the Premier League title. In a ‘mini league’ of those six sides, Liverpool are bottom in the aforementioned period.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side must prove on Sunday they can deliver in the biggest matches.

Manchester United did the double over Liverpool in the Premier League last season.

United did the double over Liverpool last season, Manchester City have beaten them four times in little over 12 months, Arsenal won on Merseyside a month ago.

According to recent reports, so why has this team gone from looking formidable 18 months ago to rather flappable whenever the historic massive boys are in town? Casual neutrals who only tune in for the showpiece Sunday 4.30pm may joke that they have not seen Liverpool play well for a good year.

A lot of the answer to that question comes back to Arne Slot and the concerns we documented every week last season, when his side were dull and boring to watch, naked in defence and would capitulate in an instant.

Maybe players like Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola thrive more in intricate spaces rather than the gaping gaps left behind by the attack-minded bigger teams.

Another reason could be the simple fact that these sides are more likely to expose Liverpool’s vulnerabilities, such as the lack of a true defensive midfielder, the poor full backs or the frailties at defending set-pieces.

Anfield has lost its fear factor somewhat, too. Liverpool are top of the Premier League away table with 13 points from 15, but 18th in the home table with just one win in five games.

Recent findings suggest that city had not won in front of a crowd there since 2003, now they have done it two seasons running. Arsenal had not triumphed at the stadium for 14 years until last month.

According to recent reports, iraola is aware of all this and said on Friday: ‘United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season.

Liverpool bemoaned Ryan Gravenberch’s red card in their home defeat to Manchester City.

The Reds spurned a number of chances when they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal last month.

It has been revealed that ‘Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

‘We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a major game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, so we want to play well and we want to win.’.

Asked if he understands the importance of the fixture to fans, Iraola – who spent the weekend off taking in grassroots football and netball games following his kids – remarked: ‘I am very aware! This is the biggest one in English football. In this country, this is the one.’.

Recent findings suggest that in Iraola’s first two bigger games, a theme threatened to emerge. Against Manchester City, Liverpool were well in the contest until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card but were toothless when it came to putting their chances away, lacking bite in attack.

The game was there to be won at 0-0, with the Anfield crowd roaring, but the Reds did not have the killer instinct to do so.

Recent findings suggest that against Arsenal, there were plenty of chances to equalise after the Gunners’ early goal but, again, goalkeeper David Raya could have put his feet up and had a cigar. A lot of territory but nothing to make the defence seriously sweat.

In both cases, Liverpool were on the receiving end of refereeing howlers. Gravenberch’s red was not a red – the first yellow should never be a booking – and Alexander Isak had a stonewall penalty turned down. ProRef has admitted errors.

In a recent development, to take a cynical view, though: in the title-winning campaign, we were rarely sat talking about referees or moaning about narrow misses or unfair results. Liverpool found ways to win and had no excuses.

Liverpool need Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to step up against the league's big boys.

Recent findings suggest that and that brings us nicely on to Sunday. It feels like the script has been written for weeks.

Indeed, after United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth and the score was read out to huge cheers at Anfield, Daily Mail Sport wrote: ‘Everyone is looking forward to United sacking Michael Carrick and then rocking up at Anfield to win 1-0 with their new manager in a few weeks.’.

It always seems to happen and it feels like United get results against rivals Liverpool and City even when they have felt close to their lowest ebb.

Industry observers note that but Liverpool and Iraola must not allow that to happen. There can be no excuses of ‘new manager bounce’, refereeing calls or fine margins come Sunday tea time.

In a recent development, isak and Wirtz simply must step up. It feels harsh that the pair, Wirtz especially, are always in the spotlight but the £125million and £116million signings have flattered to deceive against the major boys.

Both have been spectacular at times this term but need to show up when it really matters, while £123million addition Barcola is still waiting for his first Premier League goal.

Iraola has history with United. As a player, his Athletic Club side beat Sir Alex Ferguson’s great side 5-3 over two legs in Europe.

It has been revealed that ‘I remarked at the time, it was one of the best wins of my career,’ he said. 'United, I remember, were champions of the Premier League, got to the Champions League final and lost to Barcelona the year before. We honestly played much better than them.’.

Iraola has remained unbeaten against United into his managerial career, winning two and drawing four of his six meetings with them.

Overall, the former Bournemouth boss has played 38 games against ‘Big Six’ teams in the league: winning ten, drawing ten, losing 18.

Industry observers note that but a win is all that matters on Sunday and it is a chance for Liverpool to set the tempo ahead of a busy festive schedule. After already taking on the current top three, Iraola now contests two rivalries with a trip across the city to Everton next week.

Six of nine pre-Christmas games are at Anfield so there is a real chance to build a head of steam in the league, qualify for the next stage of Europe and get to the Carabao Cup semi-final.

Iraola would welcome those festive gifts but, for Liverpool fans, nothing will be sweeter than giving their old foes a good old walloping on Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As PEN International marks Imprisoned Writer Day on November 15, a memoir by 2023 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi stands as a powerful act of resistance against authoritarian regimes.

"A Woman Never Stops Fighting — My Struggle for Freedom, Democracy and Human Rights in Iran," was recently published in German and is set to be released in English in September 2027.

The autobiography "portrays how Narges actually became the woman she is today — and it also reveals the price she had to pay to become that woman," Mariam Claren, spokesperson for the Narges Mohammadi Foundation Germany told DW.

Sources indicate that mohammadi wrote the autobiography in prison: "She was constantly writing," indicates Claren, whose own mother, activist Nahid Taghavi, shared a cell with Mohammadi for two and a half years, in Iran's notorious Evin prison. "Then, in 2020, Narges was forcibly moved to another prison. All her documents were gone. And she had to start all over.".

But she managed to rewrite it all, and her texts were smuggled out of prison in fragments by fellow prisoners and visitors who risked their own safety.

In her memoir, Mohammadi recounts pivotal moments in her life, including her childhood and youth, how she started taking action against gender discrimination, political repression, the death penalty and human rights abuses, and the personal and emotional toll of her activism.

The human rights activist has been sentenced to a combined total of more than 44 years in prison and 154 lashes. For more than a decade, she has been separated from her twin children, who are now 19 years old and live in exile in France for their own protection.

Born on April 21, 1972, in Zanjan, Iran, Narges Mohammadi became politically active while studying in physics at Imam Khomeini University of Qazvin in the 1990s.

In "A Woman Never Stops Fighting," she describes how she started mountain climbing as a student, and organized mixed-gender groups dedicated to mountaineering — a controversial initiative at the time. She also helped establish an independent student organization and advocated for political reform. Her activities led to repeated harassment and arrests by authorities.

She began her journalism career in 1996, writing about Iran's student and women's movements. As her public profile grew, she became increasingly involved in Iran's civil society and human rights community.

Recent findings suggest that in 1998, she married political activist Taghi Rahmani. The couple's twins, Ali and Kiana, were born in 2006.

Over the course of her career, Mohammadi worked with some of Iran's most prominent human rights organizations and became a leading figure in the Defenders of Human Rights Centre, founded by 2003 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Shirin Ebadi.

It has been revealed that she played a key role in initiatives promoting free elections, peace and the abolition of the death penalty, especially for juvenile offenders. She also helped establish organizations supporting political prisoners and advocating for women's rights.

In a recent development, her first major prison sentence related to her human rights activities came in 2011. It marked the beginning of a cycle of arrests and prosecutions that would define much of her adult life.

In her memoir, she describes an arrest that took place in front of her young children. At one point during her imprisonment, she lost the right to call them for several months.

She also details the brutal treatment she experienced in prison, with constant interrogations, beatings and denial of medical care.

Another central focus of her activism is denouncing the psychological effects of solitary confinement, which she had previously documented with fellow inmates in her book and documentary project "White Torture.".

"When someone is subjected to physical torture, the scars, blood and infections — dreadful as they may be — serve as visible witnesses," she writes in her memoir. But, she adds, "when someone is subjected to psychological torture, no visible traces remain, and the victim cannot justify the trauma — neither to themselves nor to others. In fact, it becomes virtually impossible to even accept that one has been tortured at all, which causes the suffering to continue indefinitely.".

"This is also the goal of solitary confinement: to bring the imprisoned person to the very edge of nothingness — to strip them of their identity and of everything that makes them human," she writes.

Through her relentless campaigning against executions and state violence, she helped bring these problems to the forefront of public debate among Iranian activists.

International recognition of her work culminated in October 2023 when she was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for "for her fight against the oppression of women in Iran and her fight to promote human rights and freedom for all.".

As Mohammadi was unable to attend the ceremony because she remained imprisoned in Tehran's Evin Prison, the award was accepted on her behalf by her teenage twins, who delivered her message to the world.

Following the Nobel Prize, Iranian authorities continued to pursue upcoming legal cases against her, restrict her communications and intensify pressure on her from prison.

She became the target of a systematic smear campaign, including widespread defamation, gender-based harassment and explicit death threats.

"We are firmly convinced that the Islamic Republic of Iran has deployed its cyber army — which is the second-largest, after Russia's — to this end," notes Claren of the Narges Mohammadi Foundation. Conspiracy theorists even started claiming she might be working for the regime, she adds: "And what is truly terrible about this is that when a lie is repeated over and over again and spread over the course of years, it eventually leads even ordinary people to start believing it.".

In late 2024, following surgery, Mohammadi was granted a temporary medical release. Doctors warned at the time that a return to prison could seriously endanger her health.

Nevertheless, Mohammadi was brutally arrested again in December 2025, while attending a memorial ceremony for Khosrow Alikordi, a lawyer and human rights activist who died in suspicious circumstances.

In prison, she was held in solitary confinement for an extended period and her health continued to deteriorate, Claren reports. But "thanks to a public campaign, she has now been granted what is known as an interruption of detention for medical reasons.".

But "that doesn't mean she is free," adds Claren, who notes that she still suffers from serious health problems — as do many Iranians who have been tortured in prison.

In February, an Iranian court ordered additional prison sentences for Mohammadi, along with a travel ban.

Mohammadi lives in constant fear of having to return to prison any day, notes Claren, and "this all comes with the pressure to which Iranian civil society — including, of course, people like Narges — is currently subjected, with questions like: Will Trump launch an attack, yes or no? Will there be another war?".

Sources indicate that despite this uncertainty, Mohammadi continues her activism. Her international profile also helps her supporters keep addressing publicly the issue of human rights in Iran in the public eye, says Claren: "It is incredibly important that, alongside the individual Narges Mohammadi, the focus also remains consistently on the struggle of the people in Iran for freedom, dignity, and fundamental rights — for the right to sing and dance.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Serie A has always been one of Europe’s most competitive football leagues, with established clubs, talented players and managers who place great importance on tactics.

Inter, Juventus, Milan and Napoli regularly compete for major honours, while other teams are constantly looking for opportunities to challenge them. Transfers, injuries, managerial decisions and individual performances can all influence the league standings.

This level of competition also means that expectations can change throughout a season. The best sports betting odds reflect these developments, taking into account recent results, player availability, squad changes and the strength of upcoming opponents. For this reason, betting on Italian clubs is one of the most common choices among those who frequently engage in sports analysis.

Recent findings suggest that however, few could have predicted how quickly Como would establish themselves among Italy’s leading clubs. After returning to Serie A in 2024, they finished fourth just two seasons later and qualified for the Champions League. Under Cesc Fàbregas, the club has developed an ambitious style of play and recorded remarkable results against established European opponents.

Their progress raises an key question: what has made Como so successful, and do they have what it takes to remain competitive at the highest level?

Sources indicate that como’s transformation becomes even more impressive when considering their recent history. The club competed in Serie D in 2019, following years of financial difficulties and instability.

The arrival of Indonesian investors Robert and Michael Hartono provided the financial support needed to rebuild the organisation. Rather than focusing exclusively on immediate results, the newly introduced ownership invested in recruitment, infrastructure, and the club’s long-term development.

Their approach delivered results. Como earned promotion to Serie A for the 2024/25 campaign, ending a 21-year absence from Italy’s highest division.

The team subsequently finished tenth in its first season back before securing fourth place in 2025/26.

Several decisions helped improve the conditions for this progress:.

These foundations have allowed Como to compete against clubs with considerably longer histories at the highest level.

Fàbregas has been central to Como’s development. The former midfielder brought extensive European experience when he moved into coaching.

His approach places considerable importance on possession, positioning and intelligent movement. Rather than simply keeping the ball, Como try to create situations where players have space to receive passes and advance towards goal.

The team frequently operates in a 4-2-3-1 formation, with two central midfielders providing support during attacks and helping protect the defence.

One crucial feature is their willingness to build attacks from the goalkeeper. Defenders are encouraged to remain composed under pressure, while midfielders provide passing options.

This approach offers several advantages:.

According to recent reports, the approach carries risks, particularly when opponents press aggressively. However, Fàbregas has shown that his players can use this approach effectively against teams with greater European experience.

Although Fàbregas receives considerable attention, the team’s performances depend on players who understand their responsibilities and complement one another.

Nico Paz has become one of Como’s most influential footballers since joining from Real Madrid in 2024.

The Argentine attacking midfielder combines close control, passing accuracy and an ability to identify space between opposing defenders.

According to recent reports, his development has been particularly impressive. After recording six goals and nine assists in his first Serie A campaign, he improved to 12 goals and seven assists in the following season.

According to recent reports, paz contributes more than goals. His ability to act under pressure helps Como maintain control in advanced areas.

Several teammates have also played important roles:.

Their contributions show Como’s success doesn’t depend on a single individual.

Como’s European performances have provided particularly convincing evidence of their improvement.

Their 4-1 Champions League victory over Manchester United demonstrated how effectively they could compete against a major European club.

An even more extraordinary result followed against Lens, when Como secured a 9-1 away victory.

The victory equalled the largest winning margin in Champions League history and made Como the first away team to score nine goals in a match in the competition.

Beyond the scoreline, the performance highlighted several notable qualities.

Como created opportunities through coordinated passing, exploited defensive weaknesses and maintained their attacking organisation throughout the match.

The involvement of younger players also demonstrated the squad’s growing depth.

Industry observers note that nevertheless, exceptional results should be assessed carefully. Scoring nine goals in one match is highly unusual, and such performances cannot reasonably be expected every week.

The more notable measure is whether Como can consistently perform well against strong opposition.

The club has built a promising foundation, but staying among Serie A’s strongest teams presents different challenges than reaching that level.

It has been revealed that one major concern is squad depth. Competing in domestic and European competitions increases the demands on players, particularly those regularly involved in high-intensity matches.

Injuries and fatigue can affect performance, making reliable alternatives essential.

It has been revealed that another challenge involves retaining vital personnel. Players such as Paz are likely to attract interest from larger European clubs, while Fàbregas’ coaching achievements could generate opportunities elsewhere.

Three priorities will be particularly important:.

According to recent reports, tactical flexibility will also matter. Opponents will increasingly study Como’s methods, making it necessary for Fàbregas to develop alternatives when possession-based attacks become less effective.

Como’s development is not simply the result of significant financial investment, nor is it just another lucky streak of a team that was treated like an underdog by betting sites. Their achievements reflect effective recruitment, coaching consistency, and a clear understanding of how the team should play.

The victories over Manchester United and Lens show their potential, but long-term success will depend on delivering consistent performances over entire seasons.

Maintaining Champions League qualification will be difficult, particularly against established Italian clubs with greater experience and resources.

Even so, Como have already shown that a carefully managed club can improve rapidly without abandoning its footballing principles.

If they retain their key personnel, keep developing young players, and strengthen the squad intelligently, Como could remain among Italy’s leading teams rather than enjoy only a brief period of success.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi has made a surprising admission about his coaching future, suggesting he could step away from football management far earlier than expected despite holding a contract in North London until June 2031.
  • Speaking in a candid interview with French broadcaster Canal+ (relayed via Foot Mercato), the 47-year-old Italian revealed that the all-consuming nature of top-flight management has left him contemplating an early retirement, even though he only signed a five-year deal with Tottenham in March 2026.
  • De Zerbi explained that he no longer views winning trophies as the only measure of success.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi has made a surprising admission about his coaching future, suggesting he could step away from football management far earlier than expected despite holding a contract in North London until June 2031.

Speaking in a candid interview with French broadcaster Canal+ (relayed via Foot Mercato), the 47-year-old Italian revealed that the all-consuming nature of top-flight management has left him contemplating an early retirement, even though he only signed a five-year deal with Tottenham in March 2026.

De Zerbi explained that he no longer views winning trophies as the only measure of success.

Sources indicate that “I don’t think I’ll stay in football much longer. Your life revolves around football, but life isn’t just that.

“That time hasn’t come yet. For me, being a coach at this level is already a dream. I don’t measure dreams by the titles won, but more by the human impact you have. I always want to stay the same, always look people in the eye. Even when I make mistakes, because I make a lot of them.”.

De Zerbi did not suggest that he is planning to leave Tottenham immediately or that he intends to walk away before his current contract expires.

However, his comments indicate that he does not necessarily see himself remaining in management for another decade or more.

Despite the uncertainty surrounding his long-term ambitions, De Zerbi’s immediate focus remains on improving Tottenham’s fortunes.

The Italian arrived in North London in March 2026 and helped Spurs move away from relegation danger during the closing stages of last season.

However, the beginning of the 2026/27 campaign proved difficult despite heavy spending in the summer tranasfer window.

Tottenham failed to win any of their opening six Premier League matches, scoring just three goals during that period.

However, Tottenham’s recent form suggests the manager’s methods are beginning to produce results.

Spurs have now won four of their last five Premier League matches, including an impressive victory over Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.

Their latest win came on Saturday, when they defeated Ipswich Town 2-0 at home.

Teenage midfielder Luca Williams-Barnett, 18, played an influential role in the victory as Tottenham continued their climb up the table.

The result lifted Spurs to ninth in the Premier League standings with 15 points.

Enzo Maresca’s flawless start to the Premier League with Manchester City is over after another masterclass from Unai Emery.

Matches at Villa Park were a notoriously chastening experience for Pep Guardiola and it was the same old story for Maresca as City have now lost on their last four visits here.

Recent findings suggest that on his fourth anniversary in charge of Villa, there was more tactical brilliance from Emery, who also did the double over Guardiola last season. It was Emery’s £65m record signing Nicolas Jackson who again underlined how some managers can get the best out of certain players.

Industry observers note that jackson had been a target for Emery ever since the Basque’s appointment and now has seven goals in claret and blue. It will have been an especially sweet moment for the Senegal forward, for it was Maresca who allowed him to join Bayern Munich on loan while he was in charge at Chelsea.

City’s run of seven league wins in a row always looked in danger here against a vibrant and energetic Villa. Maresca will also reflect on two poor goals conceded after errors from Marc Guéhi and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Guéhi endured a particularly difficult afternoon and was at fault for Jackson’s stunning first goal. The centre-back has struggled in recent weeks with a bad mistake in England’s defeat by Spain and he was exposed for both Ipswich goals last week. He was replaced at half-time after a booking for a foul on the excellent Jackson.

According to recent reports, when asked if the goals were avoidable, Maresca remarked: “Absolutely, both. Sometimes you have to be a bit more lucky because we only conceded those two chances. While much of the focus will be on City’s 100 per cent start to the league coming to an end, Emery got everything right here. From his team selection to his set-up and substitutions, he outsmarted Maresca on many levels. After the game, Villa defender Matty Cash described his manager as “a tactical genius”.

Industry observers note that it was four years ago to the day that Emery grabbed this famous club by the shirt and collar and gave them an almighty shake. After a summer of much instability including many player sales, he appears to have already struck a formula with his newly assembled team.

There were a number of fine individual performances from many of the summer arrivals, such as Jackson, goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and Johan Manzambi.

Emery said: “We were very motivated and Manchester City is the best team in the world so this is the level. This year we started so poorly and we needed time to understand how we improve. The players highlighted the capacity to retrieve the level we’ve had over the last few years.

In a recent development, “Nicolas is more mature and very demanding of himself to improve. Earlier this season he was shooting over the crossbar but he is now finding the corners. There is still work to do and 11 points is not enough but we are feeling better.”.

Villa were fierce from the start and ahead after six minutes. Guéhi’s mistake was punished by John McGinn, with the ball dropping to Jackson who crashed a shot into the roof of the net.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Universities have become hotbeds of SARS-CoV-2 transmission, according to a massive analysis of more than 85,000 viral genome sequences and other data collected from people with COVID-19.
  • COVID can wake up a slew of dormant viruses inside you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Undergraduate students on university campuses played a big part in spreading viral variants during the COVID-19 pandemic.Credit: Leonard Ortiz/Digital First Media/Orange County Register/Getty.

Universities have become hotbeds of SARS-CoV-2 transmission, according to a massive analysis of more than 85,000 viral genome sequences and other data collected from people with COVID-19.

COVID can wake up a slew of dormant viruses inside you.

COVID can wake up a slew of dormant viruses inside you.

The study, published on 19 November in the journal Cell1, finds that viral transmission between 2021 and 2023 was highest in adolescents aged 15–18 in schools, undergraduates at university and residents in nursing facilities. Undergraduates, in particular, were consistently the first group to start spreading emerging genetic variants of SARS-CoV-2.

Surprisingly, however, staff members at all three types of institution had about the same risk of contracting COVID-19 as did those in their surrounding communities. So, for example, professors were about as likely to get COVID-19 from the coffee baristas in their university towns as they were to get it from a student at their university.

Recent findings suggest that the analysis is among the largest to bring together viral genomic sequences and medical data from people with COVID-19. “The scale is truly impressive,” says Bill Hanage, who studies the evolution of infectious diseases at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health in Boston, Massachusetts. “It’s an example of the depth and the detail of the picture that can be painted using the medium of population genomics.”.

In a recent development, the findings were based on data collected from COVID-19 tests taken by people in Massachusetts between November 2021 and January 2023. The genomic data allowed researchers to trace the path of SARS-CoV-2 variants that emerged over time, and to link this with epidemiological data about the study participants, such as their age and whether they had been vaccinated against COVID-19.

COVID jabs for kids: they’re safe and they work — so why is uptake so patchy?

COVID jabs for kids: they’re safe and they work — so why is uptake so patchy?

Recent findings suggest that overall, the team found that booster vaccinations helped to reduce SARS-CoV-2 transmission. This was true even for BA.1, an Omicron variant that started to circulate in Massachusetts in late 2021 — a striking result because COVID-19 vaccines at that time hadn’t yet been updated to protect against BA.1, Hanage claims. “That’s an important illustration of how vaccines, even when they’re not perfect, can still be beneficial,” he says.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 12:23 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:04 EST, 23 November 2026.

Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.

After just eight minutes, his plans were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.

A long ball from Ronald Araujo should have been dealt with easily by De Ligt, but the Dutchman found himself in no man's land, left the ball, and Alexander Isak raced clear.

That left Yoro scrambling to try to recover the situation for his side, but Isak stepped across him and he ended up fouling the Reds forward.

Referee Sam Barrott wasted no time in pulling out the red card, and United found themselves reduced to 10 men just minutes into a vital clash.

And former United defender Neville didn't hold back when it came to his analysis as he tore into the two players at fault.

Leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP.

Gary Neville torn into Manchester United duo Leny Yoro (right) and Matthijs de Ligt after the former was sent off.

Neville (pictured) questioned why the duo were playing as if they had 'never had basic training of how to play in defence'.

Recent findings suggest that 'When I saw De Ligt's name on the team sheet I have to admit I was absolutely stunned,' he stated, speaking on Sky Sports. 'And the reason I was stunned was because of this. If you'd watched him in Como four weeks ago he was very much well off it and that is just a basic ball over the top.

In a recent development, 'It's his problem to start with, Yoro can be further across, but De Ligt is miles away from it, then Yoro has to get further round, he reacts late, his anticipation is poor. It's so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these types of mistakes.

'You could argue Isak delays to make sure Yoro runs into him, but it's naivety.'.

Pochettino was left scrambling to think of ideas to tighten up the defence but, before he could bring Harry Maguire on, it was 2-0 through Florian Wirtz.

Maguire eventually came on but it felt like too little, too late.

Sources indicate that 'We saw him in Como and he has been out for a year,' Neville continued on De Ligt. 'It is really tough to come back. To have him out there in a game like this, he has been exposed. Yoro's positioning is poor, he has to be across, you have to cover your mate. It is bad all around from United.

'Michael Carrick will be watching and say that's what I was having to deal with.'.

Sources indicate that and his criticism didn't stop there. After having the chance to re-watch the incident, Neville's criticism grew even stronger.

De Ligt (left) failed to deal with a long ball as Alexander Isak (right) raced away before the foul.

Former United captain Roy Keane (pictured) added that he was 'amazed' by the errors made.

Sources indicate that 'It's as bad defending from two centre backs defending a long ball as you will see,' the former defender, who likened a return from a year out to playing after six pints of alcohol, added. 'De Ligt is well out of it - he's been out so I have some sympathy. But between them, to let the ball beat you, it's unforgivable.

'It is shocking. Whilst Man United have those types of defenders in their team, they have no chance of keeping a clean sheet.

In a recent development, 'It's basic understanding of how to play a position. It's the fundamentals. It's like these guys have never had basic training of how to play in defence.'.

Former United captain Roy Keane chimed in too, adding at half-time: 'It doesn't matter if it's a back four or back five, you do the basics right.

'I'm amazed at this level, I know he's been out a while, but it's really poor defending. He's never getting that ball.

In a recent development, 'If you're a defender you always expect the worst. Isak's done well and I actually don't think he's going to get the ball.

Recent findings suggest that 'There's no way he's (Yoro) getting the ball, it's clumsy by United. Straight ball over the top and he's in big trouble. But there's no way he's getting that ball. I know he's quick and sharp but it's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger.'.

Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even launches?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1092 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The world's tropical forests play a vital role in slowing global heating and preserving biodiversity, storing climate-damaging carbon dioxide and providing a home for an extremely large number of species — when they're intact.
  • More than 140 countries committed to halting global deforestation by the end of the decade at the 2021 UN climate change conference in Glasgow, but five years later logging continues.
  • It has been revealed that in 2024, over 8 million hectares (19 million acres) of forest were lost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The world's tropical forests play a vital role in slowing global heating and preserving biodiversity, storing climate-damaging carbon dioxide and providing a home for an extremely large number of species — when they're intact.

More than 140 countries committed to halting global deforestation by the end of the decade at the 2021 UN climate change conference in Glasgow, but five years later logging continues.

It has been revealed that in 2024, over 8 million hectares (19 million acres) of forest were lost. And since 1990, nearly 490 million hectares of forest have been wiped out.

More recently, the trend has shifted in the opposite direction. Deforestation in the Amazon region of Brazil decreased by 41% from August 2025 through 2026 to reach its lowest rate since records began.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

To ensure lasting protection, the Tropical Forest Forever Facility was released in 2025 at the COP30 climate conference in Belem, Brazil.

Because rainforests are so important for the world, the idea behind the fund was to give money to the countries where they are located to help them preserve and protect these ecosystems.

So far, these countries have made more profit through deforestation — for example, by mining natural resources on rainforest land or farming the area.

Starting in 2027, the TFFF is expected to generate the funds needed for rainforest conservation, in part via contributions from various countries. By the end of this year, a total of $10 billion (€8.9 billion) in government capital is due to flow into the fund, mainly in the form of low-interest loans.

In addition, the TFFF is expected to matter bonds to private investors, such as banks and investment firms, to raise additional funds — initially totaling about $40 billion.

Going forward, the plan is for governments to contribute a total of $25 billion to the pot, and for private donors to contribute $100 billion. The fund will then invest this money in international financial markets with the aim of generating profits.

Private investors who purchase TFFF bonds can expect to earn about 5% interest per bond per year, stated Felix Finkbeiner, the founder of the German environmental organization Plant-for-the-Planet, where he is responsible for forest conservation and advocacy.

"Private investors' capital is very well protected," Finkbeiner said, adding that any losses the TFFF might incur on the capital markets — for example, if the price of its bonds should fall — would be offset by government funds.

About 2.7% of the TFFF's profits would be set aside for countries with tropical forests.

Recent findings suggest that countries would receive $4 per year for every hectare of forest that they preserve instead of chopping down. At least 20% of these funds must be allocated to Indigenous peoples and local communities.

According to calculations by the TFFF Watch website, an independent platform launched by Plant-for-the-Planet to track investments, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, for example, would receive about $333 million for its 2024 forest stock under this system.

Sources indicate that finkbeiner said the subsidies would be paid only for intact ecosystems and not for timber plantations, with forest areas and their condition mapped and assessed using satellite imagery. Though it can sometimes be difficult to identify plantations accurately on satellite photos, he said, the technology has improved significantly over the last decade.

According to recent reports, that means any NGO or external party with access to the satellite data can check the condition of the region, providing further oversight. If forest areas are cleared or damaged, money is deducted from the total.

Another safeguard: If countries don't use the TFFF funds for rainforest conservation, their payments could be frozen for the next few years.

Sources indicate that the TFFF is supposed to invest, whenever possible, in government bonds issued by emerging and developing countries. Above all, the idea is not to invest in projects that harm the climate — such as those linked to oil, gas, or coal investments.

The TFFF concept has received plenty of support from environmental organizations, in part because it gives countries in the Global South significantly more sovereignty than traditional forms of development financing.

"For example, if the government of Ghana wants to protect its rainforest today, it usually asks the World Bank for financial assistance — and then the World Bank in [Washington] DC decides whether Ghana is allowed to do so," Finkbeiner remarked.

The TFFF fund is also designed to be immune to donor countries' backing out in the event of a change in government, for example. Once a contribution is made, the money remains in the fund for 40 years before being paid back.

Industry observers note that continuing protection is also an incentive for countries receiving money from the fund. "When a latest government comes into power that wants to cut back a little on climate protection, they will realize: We'll get more money if we protect the rainforest," mentioned Finkbeiner.

For the rainforest fund to actually get off the ground, a total of $10 billion in seed capital must be raised by the end of 2026. So far, the confirmed pledges from countries, NGOs and foundations total only $7.9 billion.

Eight countries have expressed a willingness to contribute so far, including Brazil, Indonesia, France, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.

Recent findings suggest that norway, with a pledge of $3 billion, is the largest would-be donor. However, the government in Oslo is willing to honor its commitment only if the agreed-upon total amount is in place by the end of the year.

"This deadline isn't set in stone, but otherwise the Norwegian government will have real trouble getting it through parliament," Finkbeiner said.

Sources indicate that germany's commitment must also still be approved by the parliament. The German government has pledged about €1 billion to the TFFF starting in 2027, to be paid out over 10 years.

Other countries are also considering investing in the TFFF, including Canada, China, South Korea and the United Arab Emirates.

Industry observers note that philanthropic organizations have pledged $88 million to the fund so far, including $73 million announced this week during the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. Finkbeiner remains upbeat.

"Promises like that always come at the last minute," he remarked. "I'm very optimistic that we'll secure more commitments at the COP — and in the course of December — and that we'll then reach that $10 billion.".

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kobbie Mainoo has warned his Manchester United teammates that nobody is ‘coming to save’ them as they face up to the reality of a prospective relegation battle.

Mauricio Pochettino’s reign got off to the worst possible start on Sunday as the Red Devils were thumped 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool at Anfield, leaving them second from bottom in the Premier League and without a win in nine top-flight matches since the end of August.

Roy Keane didn’t mince his words about the performance from his former club, bemoaning how the away fans were ‘applauding rubbish‘ from their team, who could’ve lost by an even greater margin only for some wasteful finishing from the home side.

Speaking to MUTV (via Manchester Evening News) after the match, Mainoo insisted that he and his teammates have the responsibility of lifting United out of their current mire and can’t be left relying on an external saviour.

Sources indicate that the midfielder said: “It’s all about character now. We’re at the lowest we’ve ever been, so no-one’s coming to save us. There’s no helping hands coming, so we’ve got to work together and lean on each other and keep working, and hopefully it will turn.

“We’re all committed. No-one’s going anywhere and we’re all leaning on each other. We all know what we have to do and we all know with the new manager we need to get behind him, keep working in training, and that’s all we can do.”.

(Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images).

Sources indicate that want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

This morning, Mainoo’s words will probably feel like empty rhetoric to Man United fans bruised by the latest humiliation in what could be a historically brutal season for the Old Trafford club.

Take away the historic name that they bear and the cold, hard facts paint a damning picture – one win and a mere eight points from 11 league games, one clean sheet and eight defeats across 16 matches in all competitions, the most goals conceded of any team in Europe’s ‘substantial five’ leagues this season (34 in total).

If a less successful club were to put up such numbers with almost a third of the campaign gone, they’d be talked about as genuine relegation contenders.

Based on their current haul, United are on course to end the season with just 28 points – the lowest tally for a team to avoid being relegated from the Premier League is Nottingham Forest with 32 in the 2023/24 campaign.

Maybe Pochettino does inspire an upturn in form just as Michael Carrick did at the start of this year (albeit the latter did so from a much higher base), and the Red Devils’ current struggles become a distant memory by the spring months.

Right now, though, the reality is that the club with the joint-most league titles in England are objectively in danger of being dragged into a battle to preserve their top-flight status unless they soon end their lengthy winless streak in the division.

Industry observers note that from the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

According to recent reports, “Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, noted of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”.

In Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

“I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa noted. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”.

Some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

According to recent reports, the same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

Konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

In a recent development, konsa, 29, has promptly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

The nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

Thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

The victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also claims plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his fresh surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

Recent findings suggest that “Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

“I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

“I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

It has been revealed that “We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”.

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

In a recent development, they kept another clean sheet and scored from a set-piece again. All is right in Arsenal’s world!

On bouncing back from defeat...

“Yeah, we’ve had a good start. Obviously, we had a bit of a blip last week against Chelsea. I don’t think we, as a team, won first and second balls enough and that’s something the manager wants us to get back to today. You’ve got to win your battles.”.

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

According to recent reports, “They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”.

“Well, we play every two-and-a-half days so we didn’t have much time to recover, so we need full energy. There are certain specific players as well that they fit really well for the game that we expect today and that’s how we start.”.

The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”.

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

Sources indicate that this is right now Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

Sources indicate that today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”.

Gyokeres has yet to score in nine appearances in all competitions this season, although he would (understandably) make the point that it’s harder to do so when you are coming off the bench late in games.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta remarked: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

“I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”.

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes stated: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”.

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform intends

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1046 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hundreds of thousands of people are expected to rally in Prague this weekend to protest the Czech government's bid to ram a bill to reform public media funding through parliament in a surprise overnight session in October.
  • The right-populist coalition headed by Prime Minister Andrej Babis fast-tracked the first of three readings of the legislation, which culminated in a vote of approval at 4:36 a.m.
  • The bill has already provoked numerous demonstrations and strikes across the country, but Sunday's gathering in the capital's Letna park is likely to be by far the largest to date.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hundreds of thousands of people are expected to rally in Prague this weekend to protest the Czech government's bid to ram a bill to reform public media funding through parliament in a surprise overnight session in October.

The right-populist coalition headed by Prime Minister Andrej Babis fast-tracked the first of three readings of the legislation, which culminated in a vote of approval at 4:36 a.m. on October 24.

The bill has already provoked numerous demonstrations and strikes across the country, but Sunday's gathering in the capital's Letna park is likely to be by far the largest to date.

Under the government's proposal, the license fee model that right now funds Czech Television (CT) and Czech Radio (CRo) would be scrapped, and the broadcasters would be funded directly from the state budget.

The three parties in the coalition — Babis's centrist ANO, the far-right SPD, and radical conservative Motorists, whose voter bases tend to be less affluent — insist that the license fee is an unfair tax.

Sources indicate that the parties argue that the new arrangement, which would see funding for CT and CRo cut by around 15% in the first year, would make the two more efficient. They also point out that several other European Union states have made similar changes.

Critics have angrily dismissed these justifications.

Opposition parties, civil society organizations and international watchdogs accuse the government of seeking to undermine the independence of the broadcasters, whose critical reporting has long irked ANO and the SPD in particular.

Analysts point out that while models in other EU states include guarantees of long-term financial stability and editorial independence, the Czech government proposal offers neither.

CT and CRo have warned that the reduced budget included in the bill will mean programming- and staff cuts.

When the first publication of the proposed bill was met with protests over the summer, Vaclav Stetka of the European Newly introduced School of Digital Studies told DW that such "dramatic budget cuts represent an act of cultural vandalism.".

There has also been condemnation of the restriction of the parliamentary debate amid the fast-tracking of the bill.

"The confrontational approach, the attempts to limit parliamentary debate and the government's rhetoric towards journalists and critics have all contributed to the public backlash," Otto Eibl, political scientist at Masaryk University in Czechia's second city Brno, told DW.

According to recent reports, the backlash was immediate. Crowds picketed parliament through the night as the government pushed through the first reading of the bill.

According to recent reports, since then, multiple rallies have taken place in cities and towns across the country. Many of these protests were led by students and joined by unions, Churches and representatives of educational and cultural institutions.

CT and CRo staff called a strike in early November, disrupting the country's TV and radio schedules.

Sunday's protest is set to up the ante.

It will take place two days before the anniversary of the start of the Velvet Revolution, which ultimately brought down communism in what was then Czechoslovakia in 1989.

The civil society group Million Moments for Democracy, which is organizing Sunday's rally, brought an estimated 300,000 onto the streets to protest during Babis's first term as prime minister in 2019 and more than 200,000 earlier this year.

The government's sudden bid to push through the proposal reflects impatience to deliver on a core pledge made ahead of the October 2025 election, as well as the longstanding ambition of the prime minister, who was stymied in his attempt to engineer control of CT's governing council during his first term in power in 2017–21.

Vaclav Stetka notes that repeated assaults on public media by Czech governments past and present reflect a particular political culture across Europe's post-communist states.

"The political elite has never accepted the independence of public media," he asserted.

In Czechia, however, the public broadcasters have earned special status as cornerstones of democracy.

That standing was forged in what became known as the "Czech TV crisis" of 2000–01, when an occupation of CT's studios by staff and mass protests forced the government of the day to back down on a bid to wrest control.

"The fight over the public service media has become a symbol of the defense of liberal democratic values and institutions," Eibl said.

As anger has swelled, the government has sought to calm the situation. Babis has mentioned that a new proposal, which would see public media funding moved off budget and editorial independence guaranteed, would be drawn up and made available for a full and open debate.

However, critics remain unimpressed, noting a lack of any detail and the fact that other members of the government appear determined to remain on course.

Million Moments for Democracy has insisted the pressure must continue.

Recent findings suggest that "Words are worth nothing," the group mentioned. "While people stand up for independent media, the government continues to act as if it owns the country.".

With little sign that the opposition will dissipate, the government faces a choice.

It has the parliamentary majority it needs to push the bill through and defeat any likely vetoes from the upper house Senate and President Petr Pavel.

Polls suggest political support for the government has been weakened and could diminish further if the protests expand to include growing frustrations over the cost of living and housing, as happened recently with student-led protests in France and other European countries.

"The real risk for the government is that the media issue becomes a lightning rod for broader dissatisfaction," remarked Martin Vokalek of the Prague-based EUROPEUM Institute for European Policy.

The PM declared that he will not attend the Velvet Revolution anniversary celebrations on November 17, which are hugely symbolic, in the hope that his absence might "calm the tense situation.".

However, there's little concern that the Czech protests could descend into violence.

Analysts note that the anger in Czechia remains tightly focused on the public media proposal and continues to be expressed in a similar way to the seismic events of the country's modern history.

"I would not expect French-style scenes," Vokalek told DW, noting that the same "large, peaceful and civic Czech protest culture," which gave the Velvet Revolution and 1993's Velvet Divorce from Slovakia their name, is still strong.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christian Pulisic has contributed to a goal every 87 minutes for Milan this season, while the Rossoneri have scored 28 goals in 12 league games, nearly a club record.

Milan secured a comfortable 5-1 win over Frosinone on Sunday, with Pulisic scoring in the second half.

The American has already scored five Serie A goals this season and, according to Gazzetta, has contributed to a goal every 87 minutes through either a goal or an assist.

He has also scored in each of his last three Serie A appearances. The only time he had a longer scoring streak for Milan was between September and October 2024, when he found the net in four consecutive matches.

Pulisic’s scintillating performances have contributed to Milan’s strong attacking displays, with eight different players scoring in Serie A so far.

The Rossoneri have scored 28 goals in 12 games; only twice in history have they achieved more: 29 under Nereo Rocco and Lajos Czeizler, who coached Milan in the 1950s.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are understood to hold a strong interest in teenage Borussia Monchengladbach sensation Wael Mohya, and the youngster could reportedly be tempted by the prospect of a move to Anfield.

It was less than 18 months ago that the Reds spent big on a German playmaker in Florian Wirtz, who’s now growing into a crucial figure in Andoni Iraola’s side following a difficult first season in England, and the Merseyside club are now being linked with one of his highly-rated compatriots.

German football reporter Christian Falk has indicated to CF Bayern Insider that Liverpool have a genuine interest in the 17-year-old and could be an ‘attractive destination’ for the player, given the club’s reputation for developing young talents.

It’s claimed that Mohya ‘could be tempted’ by a potential move to Anfield if the Reds were to come forward with a ‘concrete offer’, although persuading the Bundesliga struggles to sell their precocious starlet could be difficult.

Monchengladbach are adamant that the youngster won’t be sold in the January transfer window and ‘are in no rush to do business with any interested parties’, with Die Fohlen determined to hand onto him despite being rooted to the bottom of the table domestically.

(Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images).

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Even with his club enduring a dismal season, Mohya has performed well enough to earn a first senior call-up for Germany during this month’s international window, with Jurgen Klopp selecting him in his squad for the UEFA Nations League games against Serbia and Netherlands.

The 17-year-old didn’t play in either match, but that recognition from the ex-Liverpool manager speaks volumes for the ceiling of a player who Monchengladbach sporting director Rouven Schröder dubbed ‘a really wonderful kid’ and ‘a fantastic talent’.

The teenager has already scored eight times in 31 senior games for his club, with three goals in 12 matches so far this term, a more than respectable return for such a young player in a struggling team.

A scout report by Tactical Football Analysis has pinpointed Mohya as a dynamic playmaker who excels in finding space between defensive lines, and an ambidexterity which enables him to turn on a sixpence and glide past opposition defenders.

The presence of Wirtz and Szoboszlai at Liverpool means that the Gladbach starlet would likely have a backup role at first if he were to join the Reds in 2027, but he certainly seems to be a hugely exciting talent with a very bright future ahead of him.

If Klopp rates him sufficiently to call him into the senior Germany squad, that’ll surely resonate with Kopites who worship their former manager and place high stock in his opinions.
