Henry Pollock was at the centre of an East Midlands derby flare-up that sparked a second-half Leicester onslaught as Northampton were overpowered at a sodden Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

The incident fired up a sell-out crowd and Leicester brought what had up to that point been a drab game to life with a storming second-half performance.

Three tries in a pulverising 13-minute spell overturned a half-time deficit and put the hosts on course for a bonus-point win over their arch-rivals that took them to second place in the Prem table.

Pollock, withdrawn after 52 minutes, may wish to reflect on the wisdom of riling the Tigers in their own lair.

“That was a proper Tigers second half and a really pleasing performance,” Geoff Parling, their director of rugby, stated.

According to recent reports, “We got on the front foot and revealed our power. The way the guys problem-solved was brilliant and I’m just really pleased with the emotional energy they threw into that game.

“The way we were physically for each other – I’m really pleased.

“The challenge for us, if we want to be a title-winning team, is to play like that when it isn’t Northampton Saints. We have to play with that heart – the fire we showed in our chests – but also the calmness we showed too.

“I think if we play our game to the best of our ability we can knock over anyone.”.

It was a chastening afternoon for the champions who last won at Welford Road in January 2023.

Phil Dowson, Saints’ director of rugby, felt his side were in the contest at the interval but bemoaned the fact that they were unable to handle Leicester’s second-half power surge.

“It was a scrap. The conditions were going to dictate that. And they had some set-piece dominance which hurt us,” he said.

“That gave them a ton of energy and we didn’t seem able to respond, which was probably the most disappointing thing.

“In the second half we didn’t seem to have that same buzz about us.”.

Dowson was reluctant to blame the tunnel flare-up for the turnaround.

Industry observers note that “The fracas at the end of the half was just one of those things that happens in a derby – that happens every derby. I don’t think that’s necessarily something that triggered anything,” he mentioned.

It’s a massive day for Alex Coles, who celebrates his milestone 150th cap today.

The 27-year-old lock follows Fraser Dingwall, Rory Hutchinson and Alex Mitchell to become the fourth member of Saints’ current squad to reach 150 appearances for his boyhood club, eight years after making his debut in 2018.

Coles marks one of nine changes to Saints’ side for the Derby Day clash, with Emmanuel Iyogun, Curtis Langdon, Ed Prowse, Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock the other names coming into the forward pack.

Cleopas Kundiona retains his place in the front row while milestone man Coles joins Prowse in the second row against Tigers.

Josh Kemeny, with the 27-year-old continues at blindside flanker while Tom Pearson is set to make his first Prem appearance of the season.

Northampton Saints: J Pater; T Freeman, R Hutchinson, F Dingwall, G Hendy; F Smith, A Mitchell, E Iyogun, C Langdon, C Kundiona, A Coles, E Prowse, J Kemeny, T Pearson, H Pollock.

Replacements: R Smith, D Fischetti, I Neculai, JJ Van Der Mescht, T Lockett, C Chick, A McParland, O Sleightholme.

Parling has made five changes from the side that endured a 41-17 defeat to Pau.

Solomone Kata returns from injury to start at inside centre, with Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Jack van Poortvliet also coming into the backline to replace Ollie Hassell-Collins and Tom Whiteley respectively.

In the pack, Joe Heyes joins Archie van der Flier and Jamie Blamire who retain their places in the front row, while the second row make up of Cameron Henderson and Ollie Chessum remains unchanged.

Aaron Wainwright comes back into the starting lineup in the back row, with Finn Carnduff moving to openside flanker, with Olly Cracknell going at No 8.

Leicester: F Steward; A Radwan, W Wand, S Kata; G Hamer-Webb; B Searle, J van Poortvliet; A van der Flier, J Blamire, J Heyes, C Henderson, O Chessum, A Wainwright, F Carnduff, O Cracknell.

Replacements:  R Asiata, T Haffar, W Hurd, J Thompson, J Moro, T Whiteley, O Bailey, G Pearson.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the upcoming campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back swiftly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” mentioned Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”.

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”.

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

Breaking: Germany news: Parliament agrees on debt-laden 2027 budget

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, these updates have been closed.
  • German Chancellor Friedrich Merz got a birthday cake at the UN climate summit in Turkey this week.
  • According to recent reports, fridays for Future is taking its demands to German streets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, these updates have been closed. Below, you can review our collection of news and analysis on stories from or relating to Germany from Friday, November 13.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz got a birthday cake at the UN climate summit in Turkey this week. But he wasn't there to eat it. Meanwhile, in Berlin, climate activists marked his 71st birthday on Friday with a symbolic chocolate cake. Their message: they too want to reach that age on a livable planet.

According to recent reports, fridays for Future is taking its demands to German streets. Demonstrations were planned in more than 70 German cities on Friday, November 13.

Under the slogan "Pay your climate debt," protesters in the German capital demanded more funding for climate protection and adaptation in developing countries, alongside a global phase-out of coal, oil and gas.

Germany provided €4.7 billion ($5.2 billion) in federal budget funds for international climate financing in 2025 — below its €6 billion pledge.

According to recent reports, but the protest movement is no longer drawing the crowds it once did. In September 2019, Fridays for Future mobilized an estimated 1.4 million people across Germany. Five years later, that figure fell to around 75,000 at a comparable nationwide strike.

Sources indicate that this comes as broader youth frustration with German politics grows. "I don't feel addressed by the chancellor unfortunately," Kim, a protester in Berlin, told DW.

From military service to affordable housing and climate policy, younger Germans are questioning whether their concerns are being heard.

Industry observers note that A recent nationwide poll found that 82% of Germans believe politicians do not adequately represent young people's interests. Among 18- to 34-year-olds, just 5% trust Merz's conservatives to champion their concerns, compared with 3% for their Social Democratic coalition partners.

Merz is not the first German chancellor to miss a UN climate summit. And smaller demonstrations do not necessarily mean young Germans care less about climate change. But the contrast is striking: while the climate movement struggles to mobilize, dissatisfaction among younger voters extends well beyond environmental policy.

Julian Reichelt, formerly the editor-in-chief of Germany's top-selling tabloid Bild, states he was the target of an arson attack after his car was set on fire and largely destroyed in Berlin.

Now editor-in-chief of the right-wing online portal Nius that he co-founded, Reichelt remarked the arson attack took place in the Charlottenburg district of the German capital overnight.

It has been revealed that police confirmed the car was intentionally set alight, saying a passerby reported it shortly after 2 a.m. that morning. However, they did not name a suspect or potential personal motive at first, saying only that the fire department responded and extinguished the fire.

"It is completely clear that this was a targeted attack," Reichelt noted, calling it an "attempt at intimidation against new free media that stand up against this left-wing extremism.".

Similar arson attacks several years ago targeted cars belonging to a columnist for another Berlin newspaper, B.Z., with a left-wing group claiming responsibility in one case.

In a recent development, that said, Berlin also has a more general and fairly well documented problem with arson and vandalism targeting cars, with an average of roughly two a night being set alight in the capital city over recent years. Vandalism and insurance fraud are the most common reasons more generally.

Reichelt was fired from his prominent job at Bild in 2021 amid allegations of sexual harassment, accusations he always denied and referred to as a "smear campaign.".

Lawmakers in the Bundestag have approved reforms that will provide additional powers to Germany's domestic and external intelligence agencies.

The changes will strengthen both the external Federal Intelligence Service (BND) and domestic intelligence service the BfV, formally titled the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution.

The law passed fairly comfortably in the federal Bundestag lower house of parliament, with 309 votes in favor, 190 against and 71 abstentions.

The BfV will be granted powers beyond intelligence gathering and monitoring individuals, such as being able to secretly enter homes or take action against explosives or weapons.

In the case of the BND, it will be granted additional operational intervention powers, for instance moving to disable servers belonging to state-sponsored hacker groups abroad.

The changes aim to respond to intensified and evolving threats from foreign intelligence services and their partners, and to reduce dependency on information supplied by friendly foreign intelligence services.

Opposition parties have accused the government of abolishing or weakening the separation between the police and intelligence services — a sensitive and closely monitored distinction in German society, because of the legacy both of Adolf Hitler's Nazi regime and of the secret police services in Communist East Germany during the Cold War.

Friedrich Merz has noted during his visit to Dublin that Germany and Europe's position in future peace talks for Ukraine is "set.".

Following the talks in Abu Dhabi this week between Ukraine and Russia brokered by the US, which also involved European representatives at times, Merz noted further negotiations were now planned.

"In the coming weeks there should now be concrete peace talks in which Europe is represented," Merz told reporters in Dublin amid an informal meeting of EU leaders.

He said that "provisionally" this might involve the same "group of Europeans" who had participated in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday.

"Germany is set in there, that is completely clear," he remarked.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz's call to link EU budget negotiations to the provision of assistance to Ukraine, which faced hefty criticism at home, has found some backing amid European Political Community meetings and an AI summit in Dublin.

Merz, who has been leading the charge to find savings in the next EU budget, remarked doing so could ensure stronger contributions to helping Ukraine from all EU member states.

Estonia's Prime Minister Kristen Michal said during the meeting in Dublin that he approved of Merz's suggestion "that support for Ukraine is also a part of our core security and our core financing.".

He mentioned that members who wanted a upcoming EU budget should contribute.

Latvia's Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs, meanwhile, said he agreed completely with Merz.

"We must all pull in the same direction. All of Europe must do its part," he mentioned.

Luxembourg's Luc Frieden also stated that "we must all stand behind Ukraine" and added that collective financial commitments should be a part of this.

As the largest economy and most populous country in the EU, Germany is the largest overall contributor both to the EU budget and to assistance for Ukraine.

Countries that tend to be so-called net beneficiaries of the EU budget, rather than net contributors to it, tend to be more reticent to cut spending intends.

Hosts Ireland, in a tricky position as the holders of the rotating presidency of the EU trying to broker a deal on the next seven-year budget, stated it had concerns about adding an additional factor to the stalled talks, as the current budget's expiry at the end of 2027 starts to draw near.

"But I do understand why this is happening," Taoiseach (or prime minister) Micheal Martin noted in Dublin. "Some countries have made considerable contributions and they want all EU member states to contribute financially to the support for Ukraine.".

The right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) was critical of both the spending and the fundraising prepares in the 2027 budget, claiming without showing its workings that it would be able to do more with less by making swingeing cuts in various key areas.

Budget policy spokesman Michael Espendiller remarked the budget meant "more debts and more taxes and more burdens for the taxpayer.".

According to recent reports, he accused the Christian Democrats of breaking key election pledges by raising taxes on alcohol and tobacco. He then complained that despite this, there was not enough money for the promised electricity tax cut.

"If you put it into figures, the federal government will be taking out almost €400,000 (around $440,000) every minute in upcoming debt," Espendiller said, calling for an end to what he called a spiral of debt.

He claimed that the AfD would have able to complete its budget with new debt of just €63 billion, not roughly €210 billion, while simultaneously providing tax relief of around €44 billion.

Espendiller remarked this would be achieved with wide-reaching cuts in several core areas of spending: climate protection, contributing to the EU budget and other EU funding, asylum-related spending, international development aid, and weapons deliveries and other assistance to Ukraine.

It's unclear to what extent these proposed cuts would be feasible or legal, or what domestic or international implications they might have, or whether they'd save anything like the amount the AfD asserts in practice.

Politicians on the Bundestag budget committee burned the proverbial candle at both ends heading into Friday morning, trying to finalize details of the federal government's spending plans for 2027 before the year's end.

The session took over 15 hours, and already politicians are talking about areas where they still see room for further improvement or alteration — but the document does at least stand in such a form in which it can take effect without too many complications.

Including all spending plans, in the core budget and from the so-called "special funds" for infrastructure and military modernization, upcoming debt constitutes around a third of oultays.

In total, the blueprint is to take out upcoming debt worth just over €210 billion ($233 billion), while taking in a little less than €400 billion in taxes.

According to recent reports, that's the second-highest level of new debt in the post-war history of the Federal Republic of Germany. Even at the height of the COVID pandemic in 2021, new debt was only slightly higher, at €215.4 billion.

We'll likely be returning to the various details of and reactions to this story throughout the morning.

The environmentalist Greens took aim at Chancellor Merz for not delivering on a promise to reduce taxes on electricity in the final budget.

"The massive promise that Chancellor Merz made a few days ago, sinking electricity taxes for everyone, this promise remains a broken promise," party co-leader Britta Hasselmann said on ZDF television on Friday.

"It was possible to find a way at short notice for several other things in this budget," she noted.

"I think this demonstrates the inadequate planning and the weak leadership of the chancellor," Hasselmann stated.

She added that the CDU forcing a delay to the planned sugar tax at short notice was further evidence of the planning shortcomings.

A budget expert at the party, Sebastian Schäfer, similarly alleged a "leadership vacuum in this coalition government," saying that what was put forward was less a budget and more a "wooden shack wihtout foundations.".

The Left Party's budget policy spokesman Dietmar Bartsch has lamented a "knot garden of debt, tricks and delays," accusing the coalition of not conducting "responsible budgetary policy.".

Despite criticizing the debt levels, Bartsch also said it was "deeply unserious" to float electricity tax relief but then withdraw the initiative.

Sources indicate that he mentioned this would have cost less money than the federal government's proposal to buy a share of the arms company KNDS. He also said it was unacceptable for the center-left Social Democrats to be celebrating just because "the odd welfare cut is not happening.".

Ines Schwerdtner, co-leader of the party that firmly opposes defense spending and is at best lukewarm on NATO membership, said the record spending indicated that money was not as tight as Merz's government made out.

Sources indicate that "The debt brake is suspended for weapons, but for housing and electricity taxes they scrimp for every euro," Schwerdtner said. "The money is there, this government is just distributing it completely incorrectly.".

Schwerdtner, herself a member of the budget committed in the Bundestag, called it a "budget of naivete.".

More on this morning's top story in Berlin, the 2027 budget being signed off.

As the CDU calls for further savings, the Social Democrats say that the energy tax relief recently touted by Chancellor Friedrich Merz "would have to be financed with additional debts.".

Ahead of Thursday's marathon talks, Merz had said he hoped to introduce the tax relief amid the stress caused by concerns including the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

The SPD's Dirk Wiese said the junior coalition partners were "not disinclined to pave the way for the electricity tax relief," but not by making cuts elsewhere.

Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil of the SPD had said he did not see enough fiscal wiggle room to enable the desired tax break.

Bremen's mayor Andreas Bovenshulte, also a Social Democrat, said that while he would have welcomed the relief, other decisions meant it wasn't possible.

"For that, a serious financing source would have been required, for instance with a plastic or sugar of windfall tax," Bovenschulte said, in reference to either delayed or proposed but rejected plans to potentially increase tax revenues.

German defense industry startup Quantum Systems noted its drones were operational worldwide once again, including with the Bundeswehr military, after a cyberattack by "hostile actors" last month.

The company had announced the cyberattack on Thursday, amid reporting from the Financial Times that also said the Bundeswehr had grounded its drones from the company.

According to recent reports, "The fleet is operating normally around the globe — including Germany and the Bundeswehr," a Quantum Systems spokesperson stated in an emailed statement to the Reuters news agency. "The Bundeswehr was the only customer to ground their systems as a precaution.".

The organization, based near Munich, had earlier mentioned it uncovered an "active cyberattack" by hostile actors.

"The threat was contained thanks to the swift response of our IT and security teams in close and transparent collaboration with the authorities," it mentioned in a statement, adding there was no risk for end customers and operators using its unmanned systems.

Quantum drones are used by Ukrainian armed forces in their defensive war against Russia, among others.

"Companies at the forefront of supporting Ukraine are being targeted precisely because our work is critically relevant to customers' security," the firm stated. "Being aware of this responsibility, Quantum Systems has mitigation plans in place and strives to fulfil the highest standard of data and system security.".

Senior Christian Democrat Union (CDU) politician Matthias Middelberg appeared on ZDF television this morning to discuss the budget breakthrough.

He identified one "weak point" after the overnight negotiations.

"We have not yet saved enough, we still need to save a lot more," he mentioned.

Middelberg said that in his view the government would not be able to "collect the funds," because that would put too much tax strain on people and businesses.

Therefore, he said, "the government must make cutbacks.".

Middelberg acepted that it wasn't clear how to do this, speculating that "perhaps there are subsidies or some other things" that could be ripe to be trimmed.

He stated the leadership of the coalition government's CDU/CSU and Social Democrats would "consider this question very closely once more.".

The German government statistics agency Destatis has published new figures on insolvency filings for the month of August.

A total of 2,067 companies registered insolvencies with German courts during the month, Destatis noted, 4.4% more than in the same month in 2025.

The data operates on something of a delay, because the government tracks when courts grant the status, which can be almost three months after the initial application at times.

In a recent development, the increase has been a rolling trend this year. From January to August, 17,252 companies have filed for insolvency, 6.6% more than in the same period last year.

However, the total sum of debts forgiven in insolvency proceedings is actually quite considerably lower than in the first eight months of last year, at €25.9 billion ($28.7 billion) rather than €37.2 billion, because fewer large companies have gone bust.

More individuals are also filing for bankruptcy protection than in 2025, although the rise is somewhat less sharp. In August, 6,301 people gained insolvency protection, 2.8% more than last August. For January through August, the year-on-year increase is more modest, at 1.2%.

Moin! Here's hoping you slept more and better than the Bundestag's budget committee. Or if not, at least let's hope that you had more fun.

Its members worked towards the dawn in a session lasting over 15 hours, trying to iron out the last wrinkles in spending plans for 2027.

The proverbial white smoke emerged at around 6 in the morning in Berlin, with word of a finalized agreement.

If you were tired of talk and criticism of the "debt brake" and the "black zero" (a promise not to take any newly introduced debts) in the years following the eurozone debt crisis, rest assured we can assign such chatter to the history books for now.

The borrowing intends for 2027 — if you incorporate newly introduced debt taken out as part of so-called "special funds," for instance for the military and infrastructure, rather than as part of the core budget — are the second highest in the history of post-war Germany.

The country only took out more newly introduced debt in 2021, at the height of the COVID pandemic and even then it was very close indeed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gary Neville left Jamie Carragher in hysterics after bizarrely slapping himself in the face twice during a furious rant about Manchester United’s defenders following their humiliating 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.

Dissecting his boyhood club’s collapse in the Sky Sports studio alongside Roy Keane, Daniel Sturridge and Jamie Carragher, the former United captain reached boiling point while criticising the sluggish body language of United’s defenders.

The former England international suggested the players lacked the concentration and urgency required to compete at the highest level.

Speaking on Sky Sports, Neville mentioned:.

“I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they’ve got something fixed in here (points to his head). I never see any of them look like that. They look like that…”.

After staring blankly at the camera for several seconds, Neville suddenly shouted “Wake up!” and slapped himself across the face before repeating “Wake up!” and slapping himself a second time while bellowing, “You play for Man Utd!”.

The theatrical outburst instantly sent Carragher into hysterics on air.

Beyond the viral studio antics, Neville’s frustration stemmed from a shambolic defensive display that ruined Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge.

United’s visit to Anfield was supposed to mark the beginning of a latest chapter under Pochettino.

Instead, the Argentine’s first match in charge rapidly descended into disaster.

Following Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card, United’s backline, featuring Lisandro Martínez and Matthijs de Ligt, was carved open.

Neville expressed particular alarm at Pochettino’s decision to start De Ligt after a prolonged injury layoff, remarking on commentary that watching the Dutchman looked “like playing football after having six pints”.

Liverpool capitalised immediately, with Dominik Szoboszlai opening the scoring in the 10th minute from a free-kick.

Florian Wirtz doubled the advantage three minutes later with an acrobatic volley as United struggled to contain the home side.

The visitors’ defensive problems continued throughout the match, with Liverpool eventually securing a comprehensive 4-0 victory with Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz adding their names onto the scoresheet.

The 4-0 demolition continues a remarkable streak of one-sided results in this historic rivalry between the two clubs over the past decade.

Remarkably, it was the fifth time since October 2021 that Liverpool have beaten Manchester United by three or more goals in the Premier League.

The sequence includes the famous 7-0 demolition at Anfield in March 2023, alongside two previous 4-0 victories and a 5-0 win at Old Trafford.

The latest result was particularly damaging given United’s current standings in the Premier League and the optimism surrounding Pochettino’s arrival.

With the Reds Devils sitting 19th in the league with just one win in eleven games, they are very much in the relegation fight this season.

People entering old age now have better memory than their parents did

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Improvements in education, lifestyle and health during early life are slowing rates of cognitive decline in older people.Credit: Laura Olivas/Getty.
  • In a recent development, people born later in the twentieth century have a better memory when they enter old age and experience slower cognitive decline than do those born earlier, according to a study1 published in Nature Medicine on 17 November.
  • It has been revealed that the researchers analysed data from memory tests that required participants to recall lists of words.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Improvements in education, lifestyle and health during early life are slowing rates of cognitive decline in older people.Credit: Laura Olivas/Getty.

In a recent development, people born later in the twentieth century have a better memory when they enter old age and experience slower cognitive decline than do those born earlier, according to a study1 published in Nature Medicine on 17 November. The analysis offers clues about why dementia rates have fallen by 13% per decade over the past 27 years in Europe and the United States2.

It has been revealed that the researchers analysed data from memory tests that required participants to recall lists of words. The study included 219,000 people aged 50 and older who were born between 1910 and 1964, and tracked changes in their scores over three decades. These list-based tests are commonly used to screen for dementia and Alzheimer’s disease.

Consistent with previous studies3, people born more recently entered old age with better memory performance compared with those born in earlier generations. A ten-year jump in birth date was associated with a 10% higher memory score at the age of 60. Memory decline also seems to have become less steep across successive generations, claims study co-author Anders Fjell, a neuropsychologist at the University of Oslo in Norway.

The findings are “confirmatory” of other studies on the topic, which indicated that the rate of memory decline is slowing down but weren’t statistically significant, claims Carol Brayne, an epidemiologist who studies dementia at the University of Cambridge, UK. “It is another piece of the jigsaw.”.

It has been revealed that because many populations around the world are ageing — that is, older individuals are becoming a larger proportion of the total population — the number of people living with dementia is increasing worldwide. But an individual person’s risk of dementia at any given age has dropped by two-thirds over the past 40 years in the United States4. “For those who reach 80, a smaller percentage [of people] will get dementia than before,” explains Fjell.

Memory stays strong in old age when this brain enzyme is active.

Memory stays strong in old age when this brain enzyme is active.

Recent findings suggest that to understand what might be driving this trend, Fjell and his colleagues used longitudinal data on individuals’ cognitive performance to estimate their memory trajectories over time. The authors examined whether people born later in the twentieth century showed differences in their memory performance and their rate of memory decline compared with those born earlier.

The analysis found that with each successive birth decade, people were 64% more likely to maintain stable memory function — that is, experience little or no memory deterioration.

In a recent development, the authors also investigated brain imaging data from nearly 2,000 people over a median of four years. They found that a stable memory during ageing also corresponded to a decrease in shrinkage of the hippocampus — a brain region involved in memory formation.

Former Italian striker Paolo Di Canio feels Milan would ‘be mid-table’ with Rafael Leao this season: ‘Cisse is worth three times more, Moreira five.’.

Milan secured a 5-1 win over Frosinone on Sunday, a result that helped the Rossoneri climb to fourth in the Serie A table with four wins from their last five league matches.

Di Canio examined Milan’s victory during Sky Sport Italia’s Sunday Night Show, highlighting a substantial difference from the past.

The former Milan, Lazio, Juventus and West Ham striker has always been very critical of Rafael Leao, especially due to the Portuguese’s attitude and, last night, he reiterated (via TMW): “You massacred me for three years. This is a serious team; Cisse is already worth three times more than Leao.

Sources indicate that “Moreira is worth five times more because of his seriousness, effectiveness, quality and empathy with his teammates. Milan are a serious team. With Leao, they’d be mid-table now, with doubts.”.

Milan sold Leao to Galatasaray last summer for €38m plus a 20% sell-on clause.

They brought back Italy international Alphadjo Cisse from a loan spell at Serie B side Catanzaro and signed Diego Moreira from Strasbourg for €50m.

Di Canio went on to praise Adrien Rabiot, who has scored or assisted in each of his last seven Serie A matches, equalling Rossoneri legend Kaká.

Di Canio, however, also pointed out that Frosinone’s defence was hardly the toughest to test.

“He [Rabiot] is good, but he can play blindfolded here,” the ex-striker concluded.

Recent findings suggest that “The last eight, ten teams in Serie A defend pathetically. You go straight in goal with a vertical pass; it’s ridiculous.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Everton Football Club and Everton Disabled Supporters’ Association (EDSA) have reaffirmed their commitment to working together to improve the matchday experience for disabled supporters, following their latest quarterly meeting at Hill Dickinson Stadium.
  • The meeting, held on Wednesday 18 November at Royal Liver Building, provided an opportunity to review the progress made since the Club’s move to its new waterfront home, recognise improvements delivered through supporter feedback and identify further opportunities to enhance accessibility.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everton Football Club and Everton Disabled Supporters’ Association (EDSA) have reaffirmed their commitment to working together to improve the matchday experience for disabled supporters, following their latest quarterly meeting at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

The meeting, held on Wednesday 18 November at Royal Liver Building, provided an opportunity to review the progress made since the Club’s move to its new waterfront home, recognise improvements delivered through supporter feedback and identify further opportunities to enhance accessibility.

EDSA representatives welcomed the Club’s continued engagement and the positive changes introduced across accessible parking, ticketing and matchday services, recognising the value of regular dialogue in helping shape practical improvements.

SIGNIFICANT PROGRESS ON ACCESSIBLE PARKING.

Among the most notable improvements has been the significant expansion of accessible parking provision at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Since the beginning of the 2025/26 season, the number of parking spaces available to disabled supporters has increased, placing Everton among the Premier League clubs offering the highest number of accessible parking spaces.

Working closely with EDSA, the Club has also introduced revised traffic management arrangements in the Ten Streets area, helping more Blue Badge holders park closer to the stadium.

The introduction of dedicated parking permits, improved stewarding arrangements and managed access to Nelson Dock has further contributed to a smoother and more organised matchday experience.

EDSA members acknowledged the progress made, with the Club and supporter representatives continuing to work together to address specific traffic management challenges and further improve access.

SUPPORTER FEEDBACK DRIVING TICKETING IMPROVEMENTS.

The meeting also highlighted the positive impact of changes to accessibility ticketing, particularly the introduction of an improved resale process for disabled Season Ticket Members.

Originally proposed by EDSA through its discussions with the Club, the process allows accessible seating and wheelchair spaces to be made available to other eligible disabled supporters when Season Ticket Members are unable to attend.

The initiative has provided greater flexibility for supporters, while helping ensure that accessible spaces are utilised wherever possible.

EDSA welcomed the Club’s willingness to involve disabled supporters in developing these processes, recognising the ticket resale initiative as a positive example of how meaningful engagement can translate into practical benefits.

The Club also confirmed that EDSA will continue to be involved in discussions around Season Ticket arrangements for the 2027/28 campaign, with a dedicated meeting planned for January.

CONTINUED INVESTMENT IN MATCHDAY ACCESSIBILITY.

Beyond parking and ticketing, a range of additional improvements have been introduced across Hill Dickinson Stadium to enhance comfort, accessibility and independence.

These include the installation of low-level shelving on concourses and cup holders for Personal Assistant seats, alongside the planned introduction of Accessibility Bag Exemption Tags for supporters who need to bring essential medical or accessibility items into the stadium.

A newly introduced Access Passport has also been introduced, providing useful stadium information and enabling supporters to share individual accessibility requirements with the Club to help inform the support available to them.

Further measures are being progressed, including the provision of waterproof ponchos for supporters in exposed accessible seating areas during adverse weather.

The quarterly meeting also provided an opportunity for EDSA to raise feedback on the delivery of at-seat food and beverage services, catering options and access arrangements in certain areas of the stadium, including accessibility lift logistics for Club View Members.

The Club has committed to reviewing these matters with the relevant operational teams and catering partner Aramark, ensuring supporter feedback continues to inform improvements.

The continued focus on accessibility comes as Everton prepares to host the launch of the second edition of Level Playing Field’s Accessible Stadia Guide at Hill Dickinson Stadium later this week.

The event will provide another opportunity to highlight the importance of accessibility across football and the role clubs and disabled supporters can play in driving positive change.

Everton and EDSA will continue their regular programme of engagement, with the next quarterly meeting scheduled for February 2027.

Through this ongoing relationship, the Club remains committed to ensuring that feedback from disabled supporters plays a central role in shaping improvements and making Hill Dickinson Stadium a welcoming, accessible and inclusive home for all Evertonians.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With the controversy sparked by Felix Nmecha's celebrations after his goals in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elfersberg last weekend, the subject was always going to be top of reporters' minds when Germany coach Jürgen Klopp faced reporters ahead of Friday's match against Serbia.

Nmecha celebrated the goals by mimicking taking a crown off his head and kneeling to place it on the ground.

This was understood by many to be a nod to a Ballers in God (SUBSTANTIAL) campaign called "The King's Return.".

Industry observers note that MASSIVE, a Christian group for footballers, has remarked it aims to "demonstrate love and respect towards everyone," but critics claim it discriminates against the queer and transexual people. The discourse generated by the celebration did not go unnoticed by the Germany boss.

​Klopp told reporters in Belgrade on Thursday evening, that the 26-year-old Nmecha had assured him that he meant no harm by his actions.

Industry observers note that "Last weekend I ​saw Felix score two great goals and saw the celebration and then the gesture. I thought nothing of it at the time, but then it all kicked off," he stated.

"As the controversy escalated, I started looking into the details of the subject and trying to form a clear picture of it.

It has been revealed that "I confronted him with all the things you (reporters) might have confronted him with. He told me that it had nothing to do with that at all, and that he loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone.".

He then stated that Nmecha had agreed not to repeat the celebration.

Industry observers note that in Friday's match, Klopp's goal will be to keep alive Germany's chances of reaching the Nations League quarterfinals with a win over Serbia. Germany are third in Group A2 with 5 points, trailing the Netherlands and Greece, who both have 8. Serbia, who Germany beat 2-0 in Munich last month, are still without a win.

"We feel well prepared," Klopp said, adding that his team were committed to earning "a final" for the last group last group game on Monday in Berlin against the Netherlands.

In a recent development, klopp also expressed his disappointment that only a few thousand Serbian children would be admitted to the stadium due to a spectator ban. Originally, the game was to be played behind closed doors after Serbia was sanctioned for racist and discriminatory behavior by its fans. However, a clause in the UEFA rules allows a selected group of guests to attend. Now children under 15 accompanied by teachers or football coaches are expected to be at the match.

"We're expecting some 5,000 guests," a spokesman for the Serbian FA told the DPA news agency. The stadium's capacity is 55,000. The German FA has been allocated just 50 tickets for its fans.

The two things Roberto De Zerbi demanded from Luca Williams-Barnett's first Tottenham start as 18-year-old star eyes upcoming lucrative deal with clubs circling, writes MATT BARLOW

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:17 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.
  • De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:17 EST, 23 November 2026.

Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.

De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.

Williams-Barnett did not hide his disappointment. 'Why, do you think you are ready to start for the first team?' asked the Spurs boss. The 18-year-old remarked he thought so.

De Zerbi cracked a smile and told him he was in the team against Ipswich but demanded two things in return.

First, that his young star would play with freedom as though 'in the park with friends' and second that he would work without the ball in the manner of the world's best players in his position, such as Lamine Yamal.

This is where the comparisons to Yamal emerged soon after Williams-Barnett lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Similarities are evident in physique, his fluency of movement on the ball and the bursts of pace, the way they look to play. Even the hairstyle.

Just as Yamal, a left footer, likes to operate wide on the right for Barcelona and Spain, De Zerbi deployed Williams-Barnett as a right footer on the left, although most of his youth career has been spent centrally in the No.10 position.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored his first Premier League goal for Tottenham on his first start in the top flight.

The talented academy youngster may not be lightning fast but he has pace and creates goals.

Sources indicate that he does not possess what you would consider in modern football to be exceptional pace, but he is quick, and his strengths are on the ball. He likes the ball. He creates. And he scores goals.

From wide on the left against Ipswich, he scored within 15 minutes, darting in at the back post to finish, and created the second for Dominic Solanke, with a 60-yard run from inside his own half and cross with his left foot.

His brilliance lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there has not been a lot to celebrate in the last 18 months. Terrible home form was the crux of last season's relegation fears.

Here, they rose to salute a new talent, one of their own. One De Zerbi believes has the attitude to match his outrageous talent. Confident, certainly. Aware of his natural gifts and his technical skills. Perhaps bordering on arrogance when on the pitch.

De Zerbi was pleased to see Williams-Barnett, in a seat nearby on the team bus from the training ground to the stadium, watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar.

According to recent reports, the Spurs boss, who has faith in the power of inspirational video footage, took this as a positive sign. The youngster was relaxed but more than this he had a passion for football and always looking to learn.

'I'm positive about his character and behaviour because I've been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough,' noted De Zerbi, whose tactical instructions involved James Maddison operating closely to Williams-Barnett, a kindred spirit in a footballing sense able to talk him through the game.

When the teenager set off on the swaggering run for Solanke's goal, Maddison could be seen nearby urging him forward into the ocean of space left open by Ipswich.

It has been revealed that spurs have prioritised Premier League experience in the transfer market under De Zerbi to create a more mature dressing room environment. Signings such as Andy Robertson have been key to this.

The policy is not purely for the benefit of academy graduates stepping into the first-team environment, but it does help when it comes to setting the standards required in elite sport.

Anyone gifted enough to break into the Spurs squad will have been feted as a star through the youth development phase and well rewarded to resist others trying to lure them away.

Currently under contract until 2028, the 18-year-old has rival clubs circling if Spurs cannot pin him down.

Born and raised in Luton, Williams-Barnett comes from a strong, grounded family - which will only help as he looks to assimilate into the senior side.

Williams-Barnett is under contract until 2028 but is understood to be closing in on a lucrative new deal to tie him down because others have been circling.

It is easy for impressionable teens to become conceited in this situation. Williams-Barnett has had discipline and time-keeping problems but most at Spurs speak of a young man devoted to his football from a strong, loving family who are sure to keep him grounded.

He was born and raised in Luton, starting out in Luton Town's pre-academy to Under 10s, before Spurs paid a small fee for him.

His father Jonathan Barnett was a central midfielder in Step Three of non-league football, known as 'Jono' and playing for various clubs in the region including Dunstable Town and Arlesey Town and renowned for his passing, set pieces and with an eye for goal.

Industry observers note that although more of a dribbler, Luca grew up with football in the family, polishing his technical skills with his dad in the back garden. 'He is from a very good family and it's crucial for this type of players,' said De Zerbi.

Spurs have been here before, of course, with talented teens breaking through with N17 at their feet.

There was Mikey Moore's wonderful cameo against AZ Alkmaar after which Ange Postecoglou called for patience and commonsense, and Maddison went on TV and mentioned it was 'like having Neymar on the left wing'.

There was Jose Mourinho taking the match ball from Son Heung-min, who had just scored the most incredible solo goal against Burnley and handing it to Troy Parrott on his Premier League debut.

In a recent development, there was Mauricio Pochettino dubbing Marcus Edwards his 'Mini Messi'. Pochettino soon came to wish he had not burdened Edwards with such lavish praise.

The pitfalls are well known and progress is rarely a smooth upward trajectory. It is a balancing act between maximising potential and getting carried away.

De Zerbi is quietly confident Williams-Barnett has what it takes to handle the hype.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Arsenal will be without David Raya for their Champions League fixture against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night, but downplays fears of a serious injury for the goalkeeper.

The 31-year-old was forced off with a shoulder problem during the 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday, with Jamie Redknapp fearing that a lengthy absence for the Gunners’ number 1 would ‘change everything’ for the Premier League champions.

The Spaniard didn’t partake in his team’s open training session on Monday ahead of tomorrow night’s clash against the Bundesliga leaders, although the north Londoners will be breathing a sight of relief after the manager’s pre-match press conference today.

When asked for an update on Raya, Arteta replied (via The Independent): “He is not fit for tomorrow unfortunately but it doesn’t look too serious.

“We need some more tests tomorrow but it is quite encouraging with the pain that he was showing immediately after the action – we were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected.

“We expected something much worse, as he could almost not handle the amount of pain that he had.”.

Arteta confirmed that the Arsenal goalkeeper wouldn’t require surgery which ‘would have kept him out for months’ if it were necessitated.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

While Raya’s absence against Dortmund on Tuesday obviously comes as a blow to Arsenal, their fans will mostly be relieved that the Spaniard’s injury isn’t as serious as first feared.

The 31-year-old has been an imperious last line of defence for the Gunners once again this season, with 10 clean sheets in 16 appearances and just 10 goals conceded. Take away the outlying 3-0 defeat at Brighton in September and his concession record looks even more formidable.

Kepa Arrizabalaga is set to step in for his compatriot against a Dortmund side who have a massive-name injury casualty of their own in eight-goal top scorer Serhou Guirassy, who’s sidelined with a muscle problem and is not expected back for the Emirates Stadium showdown.

It remains to be seen exactly when Raya will be cleared to return, but the outlook certainly seems brighter for Arsenal after Arteta’s patch earlier today.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that germany's intelligence agencies have been given wide-ranging newly introduced powers.
  • Industry observers note that under the newly introduced rules, the Federal Intelligence Service (BND), Germany's foreign intelligence service, will be allowed to respond to cyberattacks by foreign powers with counterattacks of its own.
  • Under certain conditions, the agencies will also be permitted to enter homes and business premises covertly, for example, to prepare surveillance operations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that germany's intelligence agencies have been given wide-ranging newly introduced powers. The lawmakers in the Bundestag agreed to a reform package on Friday.

Industry observers note that under the newly introduced rules, the Federal Intelligence Service (BND), Germany's foreign intelligence service, will be allowed to respond to cyberattacks by foreign powers with counterattacks of its own. The range of possible measures is broad, from deleting and manipulating data to disabling entire systems and, if necessary, even destroying physical weapons such as drones that could be deployed against Germany.

Under certain conditions, the agencies will also be permitted to enter homes and business premises covertly, for example, to prepare surveillance operations. They will, however, not be allowed to use force against people. An independent oversight board is to be established to monitor the agencies.

Opposition lawmakers specializing in domestic policy warned against granting powers that are too broad.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that the president of Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA), Holger Münch this week again pointed out that today's hybrid attacks pose a new challenge to the organizations safeguarding the country's security. At his organization's annual meeting in Berlin this week, he stated the "hybrid attacks" are challenging the "separation principle," which means that the police conduct investigations while intelligence services gather information. The exchange of data between the two is permitted only under strict conditions.

According to recent reports, münch has long objected to this strict division of responsibilities. He has been calling for expanded powers for the police and closer cooperation with the domestic intelligence agency, the Office for the Protection of the Constitution, which is responsible for countering espionage and sabotage.

The separation principle results from lessons learned from the Nazi dictatorship, when the Secret State Police (Gestapo) operated largely outside judicial constraints and served as the regime's central instrument of terror, used to oppress and murder Jews, Sinti and Roma, homosexuals, communists, social democrats and many others. The Allied powers that defeated Nazi Germany in World War II then decided that the police and intelligence services should remain institutionally separate and be granted different powers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, historian Sönke Neitzel of the University of Potsdam considers the separation principle understandable in its historical context. At the BKA's autumn conference, however, he described it as "nonsense" in light of today's threat landscape and said it was no longer necessary in a country that has been a constitutional democracy for decades.

Recent findings suggest that while Neitzel considers the separation principle outdated, German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt of the center-right Christian Social Union (CSU) wants to preserve it in its essential form. In his view, even a more extensive exchange of data does not violate the principle. At the same time, however, he has made clear that he wants to transform the domestically focused Office for the Protection of the Constitution and the BND into "real intelligence services.".

This legislative reform brings Dobrindt a significant step closer to that goal. Parliament approved the interior minister's intends with the votes of the governing coalition of the conservative Christian Democratic Union and Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU) and the Social Democratic Party (SPD).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Dobrindt insisted that Germany intends to take an active approach to defending itself against cyberattacks: "Anyone who attacks us in this way must know that we are prepared to strike back. They must know that their digital infrastructure, their server infrastructure, and their software will also be targeted by us.".

Recent findings suggest that BKA President Holger Münch welcomes Dobrindt's determination and points to the growing threat posed by cyberattacks. The line between criminal and state-sponsored actors is becoming increasingly blurred, he argues. As a result, both intelligence services and law enforcement agencies face the same challenge.

To underscore the scale of the threat as he sees it, Münch cited two statistics: in the first six months of 2026, crime originating from abroad rose by 24% compared with the same period the previous year. What concerns him most is that fewer than 5% of these cases are solved. The BKA chief considers this trend more dangerous than ever: "The state's promise of security can become fragile. Confidence in the ability of its institutions to act effectively and remain steadfast is declining.".

It has been revealed that A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an key afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

According to recent reports, but Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”.

Industry observers note that and how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Francesco Pio Esposito scored a hat-trick in Inter’s dramatic 4-4 draw against Atalanta on Sunday, sparking a debate live on Italian TV between Andrea Stramaccioni and Valon Behrami: ‘You have to tell me who is better than him as a target striker.’.

Pio Esposito’s hat-trick against Atalanta, his first in Serie A, wasn’t enough for Inter to secure all three points in Bergamo, but it cemented the striker’s status as the best Italian centre-forward.

Even during the latest international break, Pio Esposito scored three goals in two Italy games, including a brace against France.

The 21-year-old now has seven goals and two assists in 14 games across all competitions with Inter this season.

His performance against Atalanta sparked a debate on Italian TV between ex-Inter coach Stramaccioni and former Serie A midfielder Behrami.

“You have to tell me who is better than Pio Esposito as a target man,” Stramaccioni said during DAZN’s post-match show on Sunday.

It has been revealed that the ex-Inter coach hit back: “He’s not a target man. Osimhen runs behind. I’m talking about players who are 1.90 meters tall, hold the ball, and play with their backs to goal. Osimhen makes runs out wide so fast he scorches the grass; what are we even talking about?

Sources indicate that “So, [Harry] Kane,” argued Behrami, sparking another quick response from Stramaccioni: “Oh, come on. Kane is practically a nine-and-a-half. Sublime technique, drops out of the box, even plays as a No.10, roams all over the pitch. I’m talking about players like Toni, in the Bierhoff mould. Maybe there’s Samu Omorodion.”.

Behrami insisted: “Sorloth? Wood?”.

“Sorloth plays as a winger,” Strama replied.

“Right, so it’s a category of its own, and Esposito is the best in it, the only one,” insisted Behrami.

Recent findings suggest that “He’s the best in the world in a category with just one player. I’ve given you five names. They’re different because they offer something more.

It has been revealed that “Esposito’s category is the category of players who are missing things from their game. He’s missing a lot of the pieces he needs to be a top player.”.

“Oh, so you’d compare Toni to Osimhen or Kane? They’re different types of centre-forward. Do you remember Skuhravy? He was that kind of centre-forward. You don’t get them anymore,” concluded Stramaccioni.

“I’m saying the big, traditional centre-forward barely exists in world football anymore. Otherwise, tell me who fits that description.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Russian Ice Hockey Federation President Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency.

"There are rules: if a team does not take the ice, it receives a forfeit loss and sanctions are imposed," Tretiak said after a presidential sports council meeting in Moscow on Thursday.

"The IIHF as a way out — either allow us to participate or, if we cannot enter Canada, move the championship, don't hold it at all, or impose sanctions on Canada.".

The threat comes after the Canadian government confirmed Wednesday that it would not allow Russian players to take part in the IIHF World Junior Championship starting on December 26 in Alberta.

Recent findings suggest that "Canada's position is unequivocal: as long as Russia continues ⁠its war of aggression ​against Ukraine, there can be no return to business as usual," Adam van Koeverden, Canada's secretary of sport, said in a statement on Wednesday. "Canada will continue to stand with Ukraine.".

Following the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling in late October, in which it stated the security concerns the IIHF cited for barring Russian teams from taking part in international tournaments was not sufficient, the world governing body pledged to work to comply with the decision.

According to recent reports, on November 8, Norway said it had been bumped from the World Juniors tournament and had been informed by the IIHF that Russia would take its place. Several other national hockey associations said they had received a revised schedule for the tournament and stated they would not play against Russia. The IIHF has not confirmed the change.

Germany has been watching developments related to the World Juniors and host nation Canada closely, as it is set to host the IIHF World Championship in Gelsenkirchen, Mannheim and Düsseldorf starting on May 14.

With several nations saying they will not play Russia and major sponsors threatening to pull out, a German government spokesman described the prospect of hosting the tournament under these conditions as "effectively impossible.".

However, Germany has ruled out taking the Canadian approach.

Ronald Rauhe, Germany's minister of state for sport, said Wednesday that refusing to grant visas was "not a solution for the [German] ice hockey federation [DEB], nor is it a solution for successfully hosting a world championship anywhere.".

At the same time, though, he expressed support for the DEB in its wish to host the tournament as planned.

"We believe that we should channel all our energy and efforts into helping sport — and ice hockey in particular — find a solution, which would, of course, entail excluding Russia from the World Championship.".

What makes things even more complicated for German officials are concerns that taking a hard-line on Russia could jeopardize Munich's chances as it bids to host the Summer Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) recently lifted its sanctions on Russian athletes and suspension of the Russian National Olympic Committee, opening the door for their return to competition despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.

The thinking goes that the IOC would expect national Olympic committees bidding to host an Olympic Games to follow its lead. The IOC is set to decide in the next few weeks whether Munich advances to the next stage of the process.

For now, though, the ball appears to be in the IIHF's court, after Ottawa confirmed its refusal to grant Russians visas to play in the World Juniors. How the dispute regarding that tournament gets resolved could go a long way to finding a solution for the men's tournament in Germany in May.

According to recent reports, has there been a better goalkeeper in the Premier League this season than Leeds United’s James Trafford? It is a question worth asking after his brilliance secured his side a point against Sunderland.

Opinions will vary, of course, but the body of evidence to back Trafford’s argument to permanently dislodge Jordan Pickford as England No 1 looked even stronger at the Stadium of Light.

After leaving Manchester City in the summer to play regularly following a frustrating season as backup, Trafford is proving to be a brilliant buy for Leeds. He is the most expensive British goalkeeper. More importantly, he is playing like it too.

It has been revealed that this was a tough examination for Leeds, who were not at their best, against a typically robust and physically challenging Sunderland who are getting back to doing the things that made them so difficult to play against last season. Regis Le Bris’ side created the better chances but were repeatedly denied by Trafford.

With the windy weather playing havoc, ruining the game as a spectacle, as both sides struggled for control of the ball, the two moments of quality came from Trafford in the first half.

Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

Industry observers note that the first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

Recent findings suggest that the second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

Robin Roefs is at it again with another notable save for Sunderland 👏 https://t.co/SJ4qWmSHBo.

Had the former Newcastle United player scored so late in the game, the home crowd’s frustration may have boiled over. The point means Le Bris’ side have still not won a league game since August and remain bottom of the table. This is proving to be a tougher second season in the top flight for Sunderland, but if they keep playing like this, they will not remain in the bottom three for much longer.

In a recent development, “It’s a positive [point],” remarked Le Bris. “The more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.”.

“It’s a positive [point], the more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s still a long journey, we know with this busy schedule playing in Europe, playing in the Carabao Cup, it’s a latest challenge for us and we need to embrace it. I think we showed this afternoon that we are in this challenge, we want to embrace it and be ourselves and we probably deserved a bit more today.”.

“I think it was a good effort from everybody so obviously we want three points from where we are in the table but keep putting up the performances like that and we’ll get some.

Industry observers note that “It’s always something we’re looking to do and Robin [Roefs] came up with some substantial saves, Omar [Alderete] coming on was really good as well and I hope my teammate’s [Nordi Mukiele] OK as well because I think that was kind of my fault. But we got the clean sheet for him so hopefully not too bad.”.

“But the table always reflects where people should be but we need to keep looking at ourselves, don’t look at other anyone else, it’s no-one else’s fault but us and we know that.”.

Sunderland were warned about “second season syndrome” and shrugged them off in the summer as they looked forward to their first European campaign for more than 50 years.

They had dismissed the gloomy pre-season predictions the previous year and had gone on to enjoy their most successful season in the top flight since the heady days of the Peter Reid era at the start of the century.

So when the “experts” told them it would be much harder this season—that they would no longer have the element of surprise and the squad would be badly stretched by the extra games in the Europa League—it was easy to ignore.

You cannot blame them. It has been a magical couple of years on Wearside where everything has gone in their favour, but reality has hit hard this season.

Sunderland are bottom of the table heading into this home game against Leeds United and have not won in the league since August.

The limp defeat at Bournemouth last weekend brought things to a head, with defender Nordi Mukiele suggesting in a post match interview that his teammates had become arrogant and had forgotten how hard they had to work last season to be successful.

There was a better performance and a decent draw away to Lech Poznan on Thursday night but Regis Le Bris’ side desperately need a win in the league.

Leeds United have been one of the story’s of the season so far and have looked dangerous in every game so far.

The return to fitness of Brian Brobbey is a significant boost for Sunderland, but I don’t think any side would like to face Leeds at the moment. The home crowd will be anxious.

Régis Le Bris has made three changes to his Sunderland side.

Brian Brobbey returns to the starting line-up after recovering from a hamstring injury, while Luke O’Nien and Nilson Angulo also come into the side.

Omar Alderete and Timur Tutierov are named among the substitutes, while Kevin Danso begins a one-match suspension following his red card at Bournemouth.

Manager Daniel Farke has made three changes to his starting line-up.

Sources indicate that jaka Bijol replaces Nico Elvedi and starts alongside Tarik Muharemovic and James Justin. Brenden Aaronson and Harry Wilson both start in place of Anton Stach and Noah Okafor, supporting Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the Leeds United attack.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Sunderland and Leeds United at the Stadium of Light.

The final game of this gameweek sees these two Northern giants lock horns once again in a very intriguing encounter, with Sunderland especially in need of three points.

Following their opening season back in the Premier League last term, Sunderland enjoyed a historic campaign, placing seventh to qualify for European competition for the first time in 53 years. Therefore, their workload for the 2025-26 season has increased, which has caused their domestic form to suffer.

Sunderland presently find themselves bottom of the top-flight table, with just one win and four points from their opening seven league matches. They’ve lost their previous four Premier League games, but a win here could lift them out of the drop zone, depending on other results at Old Trafford and Selhurst Park.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, in the Europa League, it’s a completely different story. Regis Le Bris’ side are unbeaten, earning seven points from the first nine available. They drew 1-1 with Polish outfit Lech Poznan on Thursday evening, and given the relentless juggling act of domestic and European football, they’re already back in today against a very well-drilled team.

According to recent reports, leeds have made a solid start to the season and find themselves eighth in the Premier League, having only lost one match — a narrow 2-1 defeat to Arsenal at the Emirates earlier this month. Last time out, Daniel Farke’s side drew 1-1 with Manchester United at Elland Road, meaning they’re still searching for a first Premier League win since September 14.

In a recent development, speaking in his preview, Farke said: “To win any point in this league, you always have to be on it. And you always have to be close to be perfect, especially for normal sides - not like the top two. And for that, we are very respectful. So we don’t go into the trap and think we are bigger than we are. We are just the second year back on Premier League level. And we fight for every point.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham have been tipped for a shock mid-table Premier League finish by Opta’s Supercomputer, despite an impressive tactical turnaround under head coach Roberto De Zerbi.

Despite Tottenham’s recent resurgence on the pitch, Opta’s Supercomputer does not expect the Lilywhites to come anywhere close to securing Champions League qualification this season.

Running thousands of season simulations based on underlying metrics and early-campaign results, the data analysis platform predicts that Tottenham will end the 2026/27 campaign down in 11th place, finishing with an expected total of just 51.29 points.

Even more discouragingly for North London supporters, Opta hands De Zerbi’s side a mere 6.95 per cent probability of cracking the top four and returning to Europe’s premier club competition.

Those figures make for surprising reading given Tottenham’s recent performances, with Spurs presently sitting just six points behind fourth-placed Liverpool.

Source:Opta Analyst Supercomputer.

However, data models rarely capture the human momentum of a squad clicking into gear and there are plenty of reasons to believe the Supercomputer has underestimated De Zerbi’s side.

After enduring early problems, Tottenham have now won four of their last five Premier League matches, defeating Coventry City (3-1), Chelsea (2-0), Crystal Palace (2-0), and Ipswich Town (2-0).

Also Read: ‘I don’t think I’ll stay’: De Zerbi delivers unexpected message on managerial future.

That run has taken Spurs up to 9th in the table on 15 points, leaving them just six points behind fourth-placed Liverpool with over two-thirds of the season still remaining.

With Antonín Kinský keeping four clean sheets in his last five outings and exciting young talents like 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett flourishing in De Zerbi’s fluid attacking system, Tottenham are starting to look like a top six side again and could defy Opta’s projections and mount a genuine charge for a top-six finish.

#140156. What's going on with the polar vortex?
